item.title: [7] Planckian dissipation per unit critical entropy as a coupling-free probe of the strange-metal bath
item.description:
Last authors: Dino \v{S}krgi\'c, Dejan Stojkovic

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical explanation of strange metals in cuprates (LSCO), mentioning photoemission as a probe.

Tags: #theory #strangemetal #cuprates #photoemission #stronglycorrelated

Abstract: Strange metals pair a resistivity linear in temperature with a specific heat $C/T$ rising logarithmically on cooling. We find that, if electrons scatter off a local critical bath, the coupling cancels in the ratio $Q$ of their coefficients, leaving two measurable numbers: how slowly the bath relaxes, seen in photoemission or optics, and the share of critical entropy that relaxes current. Baths form classes: $Q\le4.91$ for a conformal bath, as SYK models confirm; 9--15 for the Yukawa--SYK field; and far less for Kondo lattices. LSCO, at $Q\approx9$, exceeds the conformal bound, pointing to the Yukawa--SYK field.

item.title: [8] Proximity-Induced Giant Majorana Spin Response in a UTe2-Metal Film Heterostructure
item.description:
Last authors: Satoshi Fujimoto, Takeshi Mizushima

Authors: Jushin Tei, Makoto Shimizu, Yukio Tanaka, Satoshi Fujimoto, Takeshi Mizushima

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Proposes experimental identification of Majorana modes in heavy fermion superconductor UTe2 heterostructures via NMR.

Tags: #Majorana #unconventionalsuperconductivity #heavyfermion #UTe2 #heterostructure #NMR #experimentproposal

Abstract: We establish an experimentally accessible route to identifying Majorana surface states through their intrinsic Ising spin response, using UTe$_2$ as a concrete platform. The key is to extend the Majorana correlations into an adjacent metallic film via the superconducting proximity effect, thereby making the otherwise surface-localized response accessible to NMR measurements. Remarkably, disorder further sharpens the Majorana signature: impurity scattering suppresses the conventional $p$-wave proximity correlations while preserving the Majorana contribution, yielding a giant Ising-anisotropic enhancement of the NMR relaxation rate. This approach also offers a powerful means to distinguish among candidate pairing symmetries.

item.title: [7] Coulomb- and exchange-driven redistribution of spectral correlations
item.description:
Last authors: Zanya Gonzalez Tellez, Miguel Angel Oca\~na Bribiesca

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: DFT+U+SOC study of electronic correlations and spectral statistics in a real strongly correlated material.

Tags: #DFT #electronicstructure #stronglycorrelated #gamma-Ce #theory

Abstract: Electronic correlations reorganize not only the energies of individual electronic states but also the collective structure of the spectrum. Here, first-principles density functional theory calculations combined with random-matrix spectral statistics are used to examine this reorganization in gamma-Ce within a static spin-polarized DFT+U+SOC description. We distinguish the effects of the Coulomb interaction U from those of the exchange interaction J by analyzing nearest-neighbor spacings, reduced spacing ratios, band velocities, and band curvatures across the Ce-4f manifold. Increasing U does not produce a monotonic transition between Poisson- and Wigner-Dyson-like statistics; instead, the region of strongest level repulsion migrates across the 4f manifold as the interaction increases. Exchange produces a qualitatively different response. At fixed U, strongly repulsive and strongly clustered spectral regions coexist within the same 4f manifold even while the total spin moment and 4f occupation remain nearly unchanged. The clustering persists after resolving the spectrum into its dominant j = 5/2 and j = 7/2 components and differs strongly between calculations having the same numerical value of U-J. Within the present DFT+U+SOC description, the spectral response therefore depends on the separate Coulomb and exchange interactions and cannot be represented completely by a single effective U-J parameter. These results show that energy- and character-resolved spectral statistics expose correlation-driven electronic reorganization that is hidden by conventional integrated observables.

item.title: [7] Anisotropic Structural and Magnetic Response in Sm2Ir8Al31: Al-Sublattice Reconstruction upon Sm Substitution
item.description:
Last authors: Mingyu Xu, Weiwei Xie

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of anisotropic structural and magnetic properties in a new intermetallic quantum material.

Tags: #experiment #materials #magnetism #crystalstructure #anisotropy

Abstract: Chemical pressure plays a critical role in determining the crystal structures and physical properties of intermetallic compounds. Here, we report the synthesis, crystal structure, and physical properties of Sm$_2$Ir$_8$Al$_{31}$, a structural analog of UIr$_4$Al$_{15}$, in which the smaller 5f uranium atoms are replaced by larger 4f samarium atoms. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals a tetragonal $\sqrt{2}\times\sqrt{2}\times1$ superstructure with space group $P\bar{4}2_1m$, derived from a UIr$_4$Al$_{15}$-like average structure with space group $P4_2/nmc$. Comparison with UIr$_4$Al$_{15}$ shows that chemical pressure from U-to-Sm substitution produces a strongly anisotropic structural response rather than a uniform expansion of the Ir-Al framework. While one Ir coordination environment undergoes only modest changes, the other exhibits substantial local rearrangement. The Al sublattice primarily accommodates these structural distortions, with selected Al sites showing positional splitting, anisotropic atomic displacement ellipsoids, and partial occupancies, resulting in an Al-rich composition of approximately Sm$_2$Ir$_8$Al$_{31}$. Magnetic susceptibility measurements reveal a direction dependence, including a broad anomaly near 50 K for selected magnetic-field orientations. However, the absence of corresponding anomalies in heat capacity, electrical resistivity, and lattice parameters suggests that this feature is more consistent with an anisotropic magnetic crossover than a bulk thermodynamic phase transition. These results highlight how chemical substitution at the f-element site can induce Al-sublattice reconstruction and modify the magnetic response within a closely related Ir-Al structural framework.

item.title: [8] Confinement, registry and spin in chromium migration between graphene layers
item.description:
Last authors: Lanzhou 730000, China)

Authors: Mingguang Chen (DeepGrounding), Senfu Zhang (Key Laboratory of Magnetism, Magnetic Functional Materials, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: First-principles study of magnetic atom on/in graphene, with an indirect kagome connection.

Tags: #DFT #graphene #kagomegeometry #magneticproperties #monolayer

Abstract: We compare the migration of a single Cr atom on monolayer graphene, between AB-stacked layers and between AA-stacked layers, with one first-principles protocol (PBE+D3(BJ), one cell family, registry anchors and spin-state search). We find three main results. First, on the surface and in the AB gallery Cr stays magnetic and moves almost freely. On the surface the C-C bridge is the minimum in 4x4 and 5x5 cells, and the highest point we sample on a hop lies 10 meV above it (5x5). In the AB gallery Cr sits on the inversion centres of the bilayer, which form a kagome net, and hops between them over 15 meV with a moment of about 4.32 $\mu_B$. Second, in the AA gallery the minimum is a nonmagnetic $\eta^6$-$\eta^6$ sandwich that pulls the layers together. Leaving it requires opening the gallery and switching Cr to a moment of 4-5 $\mu_B$, so we map the path with separately relaxed spin branches. The barrier estimate is 636 meV in a 3x3 cell but 260 and 185 meV in 5x5 cells with the far-field spacing pinned and free, and it is not yet converged. At 300 K, with equal prefactors and if the spin change is not rate-limiting, Cr hops between AA layers 3-4 orders of magnitude more slowly than between AB layers, using the 5x5 AA estimates and the 3x3 AB band. These AA numbers are specific to PBE+D3: an on-site U of 1.0 eV on Cr d already makes the magnetic states the AA ground state. Third, Cr binds 246-666 meV more strongly in AA than in AB registry, so the fast AB hop requires that the layers keep their Bernal registry around Cr.

item.title: [8] Three-dimensional quantum Hall insulators in magnetic pyrochlore systems
item.description:
Last authors: Robert-Jan Slager, Claudio Castelnovo

Authors: Ze-Xun Lin, Robert-Jan Slager, Claudio Castelnovo

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical proposal for 3D Quantum Hall insulators in magnetic pyrochlores with kagome features.

Tags: #theory #topological #kagome #quantumHall #flatband #magneticmaterials

Abstract: We show that a class of pyrochlore materials provides a route to realize 3D Quantum Hall insulators, based on magnetic texture and flat band interference. We study itinerant electrons on a pyrochlore lattice Kondo-coupled to localized moments living on another interpenetrating pyrochlore lattice, with the moments forming a field-selected three-in/one-out texture. The noncoplanar texture generates complex spin-dependent hopping amplitudes and unequal local exchange energies, reconstructing the compact-localized parent flat bands into narrow bands separated by a global three-dimensional gap. The low-energy states are concentrated predominantly on kagome planes within the three-dimensional lattice, reflecting the combined effects of quantum interference and the texture-induced sublattice potential. When the lowest band is fully occupied, the response is characterized by a Chern triplet $\mathbf{C}=(1,1,1)$ and reciprocal Hall vector $\mathbf{G}_{\mathrm{H}}=(2\pi/a)(1,1,1)$, giving $\sigma_{yz}=\sigma_{zx}=\sigma_{xy}=e^2/(ha)$. The quantized bulk Hall response enforces chiral surface spectral flow, visible as noncontractible Fermi loops at the surface. Our work opens a new direction in the search for three-dimensional quantum Hall physics in magnetic pyrochlore systems, and suggests a broad design principle based on the interplay of magnetic texture and flat-band interference.

item.title: [9] Exciton-driven coherent dressing in transient absorption
item.description:
Last authors: Yang-hao Chan, Diana Y. Qiu

Authors: Jinyuan Wu, Chang Shu, Yang-hao Chan, Diana Y. Qiu

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Theoretical work directly on exciton-driven dressing effects in tr-ARPES on monolayer MoS2.

Tags: #theory #ARPES #tr-ARPES #excitons #monolayer #MoS2

Abstract: While coherent excitons have recently been observed to dress electronic states in time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (tr-ARPES), exciton-driven dressing in optical spectroscopy remains largely unexplored. This work develops a theoretical and computational approach to exciton-driven dressing effects in transient absorption spectroscopy in the time-dependent adiabatic GW formalism and derives two symmetry- and band topology-protected selections rules for exciton-dressed transient absorption, unique from tr-ARPES. We then numerically calculate exciton-dressed transient absorption spectra of monolayer MoS2 and demonstrate the selection rules and their lifting after symmetry breaking.

item.title: [9] Large superconducting diode effect indicates nonuniform triplet pairing in UTe2
item.description:
Last authors: Alex Levchenko, Alexander G. Eaton

Authors: Zheyu Wu, Daniel Shaffer, Dmitry V. Chichinadze, et al.

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental observation of large superconducting diode effect in heavy-fermion triplet superconductor UTe2.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #experiment #superconductivity #UTe2 #heavyfermion #FFLO #time-reversalsymmetrybreaking #transport

Abstract: The superconducting diode effect (SDE) is characterized by unequal critical current magnitudes for opposite-polarity current flow, owing to broken spatial-inversion and time-reversal symmetries. For a superconducting pair wavefunction to spontaneously break inversion symmetry implies the formation of Cooper pairs with nonzero momentum, yielding a nonuniform superconducting state. For singlet superconductors, the formation of such a (FFLO) state has long been understood to provide an escape from high field Pauli pair-breaking -- how and why such an effect might occur for equal spin pairing is an open question. Here we report the observation of a large SDE in bulk specimens of the three-dimensional heavy-fermion triplet superconductor UTe$_2$, with a peak diode efficiency of 33% at the high magnetic field strength of 33.6 T, representing the highest-field observation of the SDE to date. Crucially, this nonreciprocal transport is strictly confined to a narrow field regime where superconductivity coexists with a field-induced spin-polarized state near a first-order metamagnetic phase boundary. The absence of the SDE away from this slender phase-intersection argues strongly against purely extrinsic vortex pinning asymmetries. Instead, our findings indicate spontaneous inversion symmetry breaking accompanied by finite-momentum Cooper pairing. We model this behavior using a phenomenological Ginzburg-Landau theory, demonstrating that the intertwining of magnetic and triplet superconducting orders can stabilize an odd-parity FFLO state.

item.title: [8] Vortex anisotropy in chiral and nematic superconductors with strain
item.description:
Last authors: David Shuliutsky, Moshe Goldstein

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of vortex anisotropy in nematic and chiral superconductors, motivated by experiments.

Tags: #theory #superconductivity #nematicity #time-reversalsymmetrybreaking #vortexphysics

Abstract: Unconventional superconductors with a two-component order parameter support the existence of a rotational symmetry breaking nematic phase and a time-reversal symmetry breaking chiral phase. A recent experiment on 4Hb-TaS$_2$ surprisingly shows both twofold anisotropy in $H_{c2}$, which suggests nematic superconductivity, as well as isotropic vortices at low temperatures, which suggest chiral superconductivity. To resolve this apparent conundrum we write down the appropriate Ginzburg-Landau equations and develop a numerically efficient algorithm for finding vortex solutions, allowing us to study their shape and anisotropy over a broad parameter range. We also demonstrate analytically that, to leading order, the vortex anisotropy is independent of strain in the nematic case, but is linearly dependent on it in the chiral phase, providing a possible way to distinguish the two phases. Using all these results we show that, in the presence of strain, in a large parameter regime the system behaves nematically near the transition, leading to an anisotropy of $H_{c2}$, but is dominantly chiral away from the transition, leading to parametrically smaller vortex anisotropy, in line with the experiment.

item.title: [7] Spin Relaxation and Electrical Control of Spin Transport in Few-Layer T d-MoTe2
item.description:
Last authors: K. Muraki, N. Kumada

Authors: T. Wakamura, M. Hashisaka, M. Bard, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of spin transport and electrical control in few-layer 2D transition metal dichalcogenide.

Tags: #experiment #2Dmaterials #MoTe2 #spintransport #monolayer

Abstract: We report electrical tuning of spin relaxation in atomically thin $T_{\rm d}$-MoTe$_2$, a representative low-symmetry transition metal dichalcogenide. Weak antilocalization measurements reveal strong spin--orbit interaction with spin--orbit lengths of tens of nanometers, consistent with recent theoretical predictions. Despite the semimetallic nature of $T_{\rm d}$-MoTe$_2$, in the ultrathin limit the spin--orbit scattering time can be tuned electrostatically by up to threefold. We further investigate vertical electric field effects on the spin--orbit length and time, and demonstrate the modulation of the Rashba parameters. Relation between spin--orbit scattering time and the diffusion coefficient indicates that spin relaxation is governed by the D'yakonov--Perel' mechanism in both monolayer and bilayer $T_{\rm d}$-MoTe$_2$. These results establish few-layer $T_{\rm d}$-MoTe$_2$ as a platform for electrically tunable spin transport, thereby providing insight into spin relaxation in low-symmetry transition metal dichalcogenides.

Abstract: Topological spin textures such as skyrmions and bimerons offer rich physical functionalities and strong potential for future spin-based technologies. These results identify promising candidate materials for topological spin textures and establish a transferable computational framework for accelerating materials discovery of complex magnetic states in two dimensions.

item.description:
Last authors: D. Y. Xing, Wei Chen

Authors: Hai-Dong Li, Hao-Xiang Long, Gu Zhang, D. Y. Xing, Wei Chen

Abstract: Recent anyon-collider experiments have identified time-domain braiding (TDB) as a new route to probing anyonic statistics. However, how such time-domain interference responds to environmental noise remains an open question. Here we show that TDB interference is intrinsically more robust than its spatial counterpart. In conventional spatial interference, environmental noise induces phase fluctuations that accumulate throughout all paths, leading to exponential suppression of the interference as the dephasing rate increases. In TDB, by contrast, the interfering temporal paths experience largely overlapping environmental fluctuations, whose contributions cancel out in the relative phase, so that only a small nonoverlapping temporal window contributes to dephasing. As a result, TDB interference decays only algebraically with the dephasing rate, providing a new experimental hallmark for its identification. We propose a Fabry-Perot fractional quantum Hall setup in which both types of interference coexist and experience the same environmental noise, enabling a direct comparison of their dephasing behaviors. Our results establish robustness against dephasing as a fundamental advantage of TDB and suggest new opportunities for exploiting anyonic interference in noisy mesoscopic systems.

item.description:
Last authors: Wang Yao, Chen Hu

Authors: Yixuan Liu, Shiyu Peng, Yifan Wang, Peiyao Qin, Wang Yao, Chen Hu

Why: Important study on exciton-phonon coupling in moire heterobilayers relevant to correlated systems.

Tags: #moire #exciton #phonon

Abstract: Exciton-phonon coupling (ExPC) governs energy relaxation and exciton dynamics in photoexcited quantum materials. Recent advances have revealed rich and tunable excitonic phenomena in moir\'e superlattices, yet the microscopic mechanisms underlying the coupling between moir\'e excitons and moir\'e phonons remain elusive. Here, we develop a real-space representation for moir\'e ExPC based on a unified theoretical framework combining the many-body Bethe-Salpeter equation with phonon perturbation theory. Furthermore, we uncover a general real-space selection rule: the spatial matching of a moir\'e exciton's electron and hole densities with the moir\'e-phonon-induced potential perturbations determines their individual coupling contributions, while coherent interference between the electron and hole contributions controls the total ExPC. We demonstrate this rule in prototypical WSe2/WS2 moir\'e heterobilayers, revealing pronounced exciton- and phonon-mode-dependent coupling, including nearly complete suppression of ExPC through destructive electron-hole interference. These findings establish the internal electron-hole spatial configuration of moir\'e excitons as a key degree of freedom governing the strength and mode selectivity of their coupling to moir\'e phonons, opening opportunities to engineer ExPC through spatially tailored moir\'e potentials.

Why: Neutron scattering study on magnetic order in a quantum material.

Abstract: In rare-earth compounds, the interplay between geometric frustration and unusual single-ion anisotropy caused by the crystal electric field often leads to exotic magnetic phases. Here, we investigate the magnetic properties of the rare-earth Shastry-Sutherland compound Er$_2$Be$_2$GeO$_7$ using bulk measurements and neutron scattering down to sub-Kelvin temperatures. A $k=(0,0,0)$ stripe-like antiferromagnetic order with locally tilted Er$^{3+}$ moments is revealed by time-of-flight neutron powder diffraction, accompanied with a $\lambda$-shape specific-heat anomaly at $T_N=0.84$ K. The temperature dependence of the magnetic peak intensity corresponding to the ordered moment of Er$^{3+}$ approximates to the two-dimensional Ising universality class. Thermal- and cold-neutron inelastic scattering experiments demonstrate that the strong Ising anisotropy originates from the local crystal electric field, and reveal gapped magnetic excitations with weak dispersion in the ordered state. Mean-field random-phase approximation with inequivalent nearest-neighbor couplings accounts well for the collective excitations, while classical Monte Carlo simulations yield the fractional $1/4$ and $1/2$ magnetization plateaus. Our work provides a comprehensive description of the spin correlations in Er$_2$Be$_2$GeO$_7$ with a particular focus on the classical origin of its fractional magnetization plateaus.

item.description:
Last authors: Maxim Dzero, Brian M. Andersen

Abstract: We theoretically analyze the spin-polarized tunneling between SmB$_6$ tip and the bicollinear antiferromagnet Fe$_{1+x}$Te. However, Bi-2212 is strongly anisotropic, and it is challenging to find its crystal axes in flakes in advance, which limits device engineering. Abstract: In non-centrosymmetric bulk materials, electrons flowing in the opposite directions often exhibit different properties. This diode-like effect (i.e., non-reciprocal electron transport) typically originates from relativistic spin-orbit coupling, and its amplitude scales with external magnetic field or magnetization in ferromagnets. Although such rectification is usually absent in antiferromagnets at zero field, recent theories predict that non-coplanar antiferromagnetic order can host large non-reciprocity even without spin-orbit coupling, magnetization or external magnetic fields. This phenomenon - the spontaneous topological diode effect - can potentially be used for efficient electrical readout of antiferromagnetic domains, while it has not been verified for real materials. Here, we report the observation of this effect in a chiral-lattice non-coplanar antiferromagnet CoTa3S6. Nonlinear resistivity measurements reveal the non reciprocal nature of electron transport along the [001] direction at zero field. The observed non-reciprocity exceeds that in typical ferromagnets, whose amplitude is governed by antiferromagnetic order parameter rather than magnetization. First-principles calculations show that the non-coplanar antiferromagnetic order induces asymmetric band dispersions even without spin-orbit coupling, establishing the non-relativistic origin of the observed response. The present findings demonstrate a new mechanism for efficient electrical readout of antiferromagnetic domains, and highlight non-coplanar antiferromagnets as a promising material platform for realizing ferromagnet-like functional responses without relying on spin-orbit coupling or magnetization.

Last authors: Zheng Wei, Su-Peng Kou

Authors: Xin-Ran Ma, Kui Cao, Qian Du, Zheng Wei, Su-Peng Kou

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical investigation of chiral edge states and dissipation in Chern insulators, highly relevant to topological physics.

Tags: #topologicalinsulator #Cherninsulator #theory #edgestates

Abstract: Boundary dissipation can reshape the spatial profiles and decay properties of topological edge modes in Chern insulators. We develop a microscopic boundary-channel framework to explain their decay mechanisms and determine the effective decay rates in the weak- and strong-loss regimes. By retaining the lossy outer orbitals and a normalized edge state of the Hermitian inner system, we identify a directly coupled bright boundary channel, while incorporating the remaining inner states through a Feshbach self-energy. In the Qi--Wu--Zhang model, weak-loss decay is governed to leading order by the original edge state's probability weight on the lossy boundary, with coupling-induced corrections starting at cubic order. At strong loss, the reconstructed inner-edge state instead decays through virtual coupling to the damped bright channel, giving a rate proportional to the squared microscopic coupling and inversely proportional to the bare loss. The Haldane model shows that the same leading decay mechanism holds for a different intercell hopping structure, while additional matrix-valued self-energy feedback modifies the boundary spectrum at finite loss and shifts the exceptional-point threshold. These results provide a unified microscopic description of boundary-state reconstruction and its decay mechanisms, offering testable predictions to guide experiments in photonic crystals, phononic crystals, and topolectrical circuits.

item.title: [9] Hydrodynamic fluctuations in Luttinger liquids
item.description:
Last authors: Alex Levchenko

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Develops theory of hydrodynamic fluctuations and transport in Luttinger liquids, a direct user interest.

Tags: #Luttingerliquid #quasi-1Dmaterial #theory #quantumtransport

Abstract: We develop the theory of hydrodynamic fluctuations for one-dimensional quantum liquids. At low temperatures the relaxation of interacting electrons in a single-channel wire separates into two classes: equilibration, which changes the numbers of right and left movers through backscattering and is exponentially slow, and thermalization, which redistributes energy and momentum at a fixed number of movers at a power-law rate. This separation of time scales gives the electron liquid a two-fluid description analogous to superfluid $^4$He, with the zero mode of the Luttinger liquid as the superfluid component and the gas of thermal excitations as the normal component. Using Onsager reciprocity and the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, we add Langevin fluxes to the two-fluid hydrodynamic equations, including a mutual-friction noise generated by rare backscattering events that has no counterpart in helium. We apply the theory to Coulomb-coupled quantum wires and calculate the dynamic structure factors, which contain a second-sound peak next to the plasmon doublet; the Coulomb drag resistivity, where intrawire equilibration acts as a bottleneck and turns the hydrodynamic drag into an activated temperature dependence; and the near-field heat transfer between the wires. Mode frequencies, spectral weights, linewidths, and the crossover scales of the transport coefficients are expressed through the thermodynamic properties of the liquid and a few dissipative coefficients, providing spectroscopic and transport probes of two-fluid behavior in one-dimensional quantum systems.

item.title: [8] Point-contact spectroscopy of electron-phonon interactions and anisotropy of superconducting energy gaps in 2H-NbSe2
item.description:
Last authors: N. L. Bobrov, L. V. Tiutrina, S. B. Feodos'ev, V. V. Fisun

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental point-contact spectroscopy of electron-phonon interactions and gap anisotropy in a relevant superconductor.

Tags: #superconductivity #electron-phononcoupling #spectroscopy #2Dmaterial #NbSe2

Abstract: The superconducting state of $2H-NbS{{e}_{2}}$ was studied using point contacts for two main orientations of the contact axis relative to the principal crystallographic orientations: along the $c$-axis and in the $ab$ plane. For contacts oriented in the $ab$ plane, dependencies proportional to the electron-phonon interaction function were obtained, which agree perfectly with the theoretical calculation. It was found that the features on the experimental curves associated with the electron-phonon interaction extend to energies twice the cutoff energy of the phonon spectrum and have an amplitude of the same order of magnitude throughout the entire energy range. It has been theoretically demonstrated that the features at energies exceeding the boundaries of the phonon density of states are caused by two-phonon scattering processes of non-equilibrium phonons on Andreev electrons. A criterion for the undisturbed nature of the crystal lattice in the region where gap features form has been found. Using $2H-NbS{{e}_{2}}-Cu$ heterocontacts in the superconducting state, a study of energy gaps was conducted for two orientations of the $NbS{e_2}$ crystal: along the $c$-axis and in the $ab$ plane. It was found that the superconducting energy gaps are anisotropic; specifically, three gaps were identified in the $ab$ plane, whereas only two were observed in the $c$ direction.

item.title: [8] Superconductivity and local stacking polymorphism in LaNiGa2 thin films
item.description:
Last authors: Xiaoying Xu, Yufan Li

Authors: Pengcheng Wang, Qingxiao Wang, Yameng Wu, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of superconductivity and local structure in LaNiGa2, a candidate unconventional superconductor.

Tags: #superconductivity #unconventionalsuperconductivity #time-reversalsymmetrybreaking #thinfilms #transport

Abstract: LaNiGa2 has attracted considerable interest as a candidate unconventional superconductor, particularly due to its reported time-reversal symmetry breaking and nonsymmorphic crystal structure hosting symmetry-protected electronic band degeneracies. Here, we report the growth and characterization of superconducting LaNiGa2 thin films on MgO substrates by magnetron sputtering. X-ray diffraction reveals highly crystalline, (010)-oriented films with well-defined in-plane alignment and rotational twinning. Electrical transport measurements establish superconductivity with a transition temperature of approximately 1 K. Atomic-resolution transmission electron microscopy reveals local variations in crystallographic orientation and interlayer stacking, with a predominantly Cmcm structure containing minority Cmmm regions. The coexistence of these closely related structures reveals local stacking polymorphism that is difficult to distinguish using conventional X-ray diffraction. These findings establish a superconducting LaNiGa2 thin-film platform and provide new insight into the local crystal structure of a material whose electronic properties and superconducting pairing remain under active investigation.

item.title: [8] Unconventional SOC-activated Altermagnetic Spin Splitting and Half-Angle Locking of Spin Transport
item.description:
Last authors: Jianhui Zhou, Rui Wang

Authors: Weiwei Chen, Ziyu Zhou, Pan Gao, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of altermagnetic spin splitting in alpha-MnTe, a key material class for electronic structure studies.

Tags: #altermagnet #alpha-MnTe #electronicstructure

Abstract: Conventional altermagnetic spin splitting arises from staggered exchange and sublattice-dependent anisotropic hopping without requiring spin-orbit coupling (SOC). Here we derive a low-energy effective model showing that SOC and staggered exchange can jointly activate additional spin splitting on momentum planes where the nonrelativistic contribution vanishes. In hexagonal $\alpha$-MnTe, this SOC-activated contribution produces d-wave spin splitting near $\Gamma$ with out-of-plane spin polarization. Its leading angular pattern counter-rotates by half the in-plane N\'eel-vector rotation angle. First-principles spin-transport calculations reveal a corresponding approximate half-angle locking between the N\'eel-vector orientation and the electric-field directions maximizing the signed longitudinal and transverse spin conductivities. Analytical transport calculations based on the effective model trace this locking to the same angular coupling between momentum and the N\'eel vector that governs the spin-splitting pattern. Our findings connect the microscopic mechanism of SOC-activated altermagnetic spin splitting to directional spin transport, providing a theoretical basis for probing N\'eel-vector orientation and controlling spin-current generation.

item.description:
Last authors: Jeil Jung, S{\o}ren Ulstrup

Authors: Zhihao Jiang, Dongkyu Lee, Alfred J. H. Jones, et al.

Published as: Advanced Electronic Materials DOI

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Direct hit: microARPES study of flat bands and gated electronic structure in twisted double bilayer graphene.

Tags: #ARPES #graphene #moire #flat-bands

Abstract: Application of a finite electric field and small twist angle between two graphene bilayers leads to widely tunable electronic structures that support emergent phenomena. Here, we measure the electronic structure of twisted double bilayer graphene with twist angles of 3.1$^{\circ}$ and 6.0$^{\circ}$ using micro-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (microARPES) on \textit{in situ} gated samples. At a twist angle of 6.0$^{\circ}$, we find that the dispersion around the valence and conduction band extrema is unchanged compared to separate graphene bilayers, whereas electric field tunable hybridisation gaps and band flattening effects occur at higher binding energies. In the 3.1$^{\circ}$ structure, we find that the resulting superlattice drives dispersion changes around the valence and conduction band edges. Increasing the gate-induced doping in the bottom bilayer leads to the formation of flat bands between the valence band maximum in the bottom bilayer and conduction band minimum in the top bilayer. Our experiments establish combinations of twist angle and electric field that potentially support strong electron-hole excitations and that provide a benchmark for the theoretical description of moderately twisted double bilayer graphene.

item.title: [7] Topological Criticality with Charge-\(3e\) Fluctuations in the \(SU(3)\) Triangular-Lattice Hofstadter--Hubbard Model
item.description:
Last authors: Ya-Hui Zhang, Xue-Yang Song

Authors: Yang Liu, Ya-Hui Zhang, Xue-Yang Song

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory of topological transitions relevant to moire tMoTe2 and fractional quantum Hall systems.

Tags: #moire #tMoTe2 #topological #quantum-Hall

Abstract: A transition between an integer quantum Hall insulator and a chiral spin liquid can become critical without closing the single-electron gap, raising the question of which composite excitations govern the change in topological order. We investigate this question in the \(\mathrm{SU}(3)\) triangular-lattice Hofstadter--Hubbard model at one particle per site and magnetic flux \(\pi/3\) per triangle. Using infinite density matrix renormalization group calculations, we identify a weak-coupling integer quantum Hall phase and an interaction-driven \(\mathrm{SU}(3)_1\) chiral spin liquid. Near the transition, both the neutral and charge-\(3e\) correlation lengths increase substantially, whereas the single-electron correlation length remains short, providing evidence for a Chern--Simons--Higgs critical theory, where a gauge-invariant monopole carries the quantum numbers of a fermionic \(\mathrm{SU}(3)\)-singlet trion. We discuss the implications for doping the system and recent experiments on doping \(\nu=-2/3\) fractional quantum anomalous Hall in tMoTe\(_2\).

item.description:
Last authors: F. Malte Grosche, Alexander G. Eaton

Authors: Zheyu Wu, Hanyi Chen, Mengmeng Long, et al.

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: High-field study of UTe2, a critical candidate for topological superconductivity and a major heavy fermion material.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #experiment #UTe2 #superconductivity #heavy-fermion

Abstract: The heavy fermion metamagnet uranium ditelluride possesses two distinct magnetic field-induced superconducting states. One of these superconductive phases resides at magnetic fields immediately below a first-order metamagnetic transition to a field-polarized paramagnetic state at a field strength $H_m$, while the other exists predominantly above $H_m$. However, little is known about the microscopic properties of this polarized paramagnetic state. Here we report pulsed magnetic field measurements tracking the evolution of $H_m$ for polar and azimuthal inclinations of the magnetic field in the vicinity of the crystallographic $b-a$ plane. We uncover a region of the phase diagram at high fields > 50 T with a ripple-like non-monotonic dependence of $H_m$ on the orientation of field. Within this ripple in the metamagnetic transition surface, $H_m$ exhibits an anomalous temperature dependence, implying that here the polarized state has a lower entropy than the low field paramagnetic state. Our results point towards the presence of complex magnetic interactions and possible magnetic sub-phases at high magnetic fields in UTe$_2$, which may have important implications for the manifestation of exotic field-induced superconductivity.

item.description:
Last authors: Fernando de Juan, Adolfo G. Grushin

Authors: Valentin Leeb, Peru d'Ornellas, Fernando de Juan, Adolfo G. Grushin

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Direct hit: altermagnetism, surface states in Dirac semimetals (CuMnAs), and explicit predictions for spin-ARPES observables.

Tags: #theory #ARPES #altermagnetism #Dirac-semimetal

Abstract: Altermagnetism (AM) and its associated spin-transport phenomena are typically linked to spin-split electronic band structures in bulk materials. However, the crystal surface has a reduced symmetry with respect to the bulk, which can induce AM at the surface of conventional antiferromagnets (AFMs) $\unicode{x2013}$ a local effect which cannot be detected using bulk properties. In this work we define the symmetry conditions necessary for surface AM and show how it can be topologically protected, rendering it a robust effect. We provide a minimal model for one trivial and two topological examples of surface AM. We show that the spin spectral density, accessible by spin- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, can exhibit a $d$-wave-like altermagnetic character at the surface, even when the full band structure is completely spin degenerate. Our topological model describes the Dirac semimetal CuMnAs, which provides an existing realization of our theory. Our results identify crystal surfaces as a platform to realize robust, topology- and symmetry-driven unconventional magnetism beyond the bulk classification of magnetic materials.

item.description:
Last authors: Antoine Georges, Miguel Morales

Authors: Chia-Nan Yeh, Francesco Petocchi, Alexander Hampel, et al.

Why: Advanced ab initio method for correlated metals (LaNiO3) with quantitative comparisons to ARPES mass enhancements.

Tags: #theory #ARPES #correlated-electrons #DMFT

Abstract: First-principles descriptions of correlated quantum materials require a simultaneous treatment of strong local many-body effects and nonlocal dynamical screening. We present an efficient fully self-consistent implementation of $GW$+EDMFT that combines nonlocal correlations at the $GW$ level with a non-perturbative treatment of local correlations within extended dynamical mean-field theory (EDMFT), with a well-defined double-counting correction and a self-consistently determined impurity interaction. Self-consistency in both the Green's function and the dynamically screened interaction is essential for describing screening processes across energy scales. A key ingredient that makes it computationally feasible is the compression of two-particle correlation functions using interpolative separable density fitting (ISDF). Applying the scheme to the Mott insulator SrMnO$_3$ and the correlated metal LaNiO$_3$, we show that the self-consistent effective local interaction resolves the overscreening inherent to constrained-RPA approaches. For SrMnO$_3$, this stabilizes a Mott-insulating state in quantitative agreement with experiment, while for LaNiO$_3$ local EDMFT corrections yield a quasiparticle mass enhancement consistent with ARPES. These results establish fully self-consistent $GW$+EDMFT as a reliable \emph{ab initio} framework for strongly correlated quantum materials.

item.title: [7] Vortex Dynamics Driven Transverse Transport in Superconducting Thin Films
item.description:
Last authors: Jagadeesh S. Moodera, Dhavala Suri

Authors: Laxmipriya Nanda, Sohini Guin, Yasen Hou, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental transport study on unconventional superconductor heterostructures (Ni/Bi), relevant to broad superconductivity interests.

Tags: #experiment #superconductivity #transport

Abstract: The generation of transverse voltage in superconducting thin films carrying a longitudinal current has been recently related to demonstrate exotic, symmetry-breaking transport phenomena. To understand the underlying phenomenon we chose two distinctly different systems to investigate; a conventional (Nb) and a nonconventional (Ni/Bi bilayer) superconductor. A systematic study of this transverse response in these type-II superconducting thin films we aimed towards establishing its microscopic origin. Both longitudinal and transverse magneto transport measurements were carried out with Hall-bar patterned devices as a function of temperature with magnetic field applied out-of-plane. In both systems, a sharp, field antisymmetric transverse resistance emerges in the superconducting transition region, closely following the field derivative of the longitudinal resistance while it was vanishingly small or absent in the fully superconducting or normal states. Based on the vortex-flow model, the behavior could be quantitatively attributed as the transverse voltage arising due to the motion of Abrikosov vortices under a combined action of Magnus like force and viscous drag force, rather than from any exotic or intrinsic Hall-type mechanism. The close correspondence between a nominally conventional superconductor Nb and an unconventional superconductor heterostructure incorporating a ferromagnetic layer indicates that the vortex dynamics alone, independent of magnetic proximity effects or unconventional pairing, seems to be sufficient to account for the observed transverse signal. Our observations while seems to provide a quantitative, material-independent model for interpreting transverse voltages in superconducting films, raises the concerns in attributing such signals to exotic physics without first ruling out conventional vortex-flow contributions.

item.title: [8] Symmetry-resolved superconducting diode response
item.description:
Last authors: Jie Wu, Congjun Wu

Authors: Qiong Qin, Jie Wu, Congjun Wu

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Framework linking superconducting diode effect to nematicity and electronic structure, highly relevant to current SC topics.

Tags: #theory #superconductivity #nematicity #electronic-structure

Abstract: The superconducting diode effect manifests as nonreciprocal properties of critical currents, yet a systematic tensorial framework for its symmetry-governed responses remains lacking. We develop such a framework by relating the angular harmonics of critical currents to the magnetic field. Crystalline symmetries constrain the dipolar response to be purely antisymmetric (Hall-like) in Rashba superconductors with $C_{3v}$, $C_{4v}$, or $C_{6v}$ symmetry, whereas they require a diagonal, traceless tensor in Dresselhaus superconductors with $D_{2d}$ symmetry. For systems with fourfold symmetry, the octupole response appears at linear order, whose response tensors take symmetric off-diagonal and identity forms for $C_{4v}$ and $D_{2d}$ symmetries, respectively. Furthermore, nematicity activates otherwise forbidden tensor components, providing a sensitive probe of rotational symmetry breaking in superconductors. At cubic order in the magnetic field, the nonlinear response tensors likewise exhibit distinct symmetry-dependent patterns. Our framework establishes a symmetry-resolved characterization of the superconducting diode effect and provides a route to probing the underlying electronic structure and symmetry-breaking orders.

item.title: [7] Revisiting spin Hamiltonian parameters in a Kitaev material via Bayesian optimization of magnetization curves
item.description:
Last authors: Kazuyoshi Yoshimi, Youhei Yamaji

Authors: Takahiro Misawa, Ryo Tamura, Kazuyoshi Yoshimi, Youhei Yamaji

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Quantitative study of alpha-RuCl3, a major material in the field of Kitaev physics and quantum magnetism.

Tags: #theory #Kitaev-physics #quantum-magnetism #RuCl3

Abstract: Determining the spin Hamiltonian of a magnetic compound is crucial for understanding its magnetic properties. A standard approach is to derive model parameters from ab initio calculations based on the crystal structure. However, the resulting Hamiltonian can depend sensitively on methodological details of the ab initio procedure. This issue is particularly evident in $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$, a candidate Kitaev material. Here, we present an alternative, data-driven approach to determine the spin Hamiltonian parameters of $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$ by Bayesian optimization of experimental magnetization curves along the $b$- and $c$-axis directions. We optimize five parameters, namely the Kitaev interaction $K$, off-diagonal interactions $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma'$, the Heisenberg interaction $J$, and the $c$-axis $g$-factor $g_c$. The parameter set that minimizes the cost function is $(K,\Gamma,\Gamma',J,g_c)=(-6.0, 7.5, -0.3, -1.75, 2.3)$, where the exchange couplings are in meV. We find that the cost function is insensitive to the absolute value of the Kitaev coupling $K$. Thus, the magnetization data alone do not determine its energy scale. The cost function also depends only weakly on $\Gamma'$ and $J$, while the optimization favors a large positive $\Gamma$. By computing the static spin structure factor, magnetic susceptibility, and specific heat, we show that these quantities favor the large-$\Gamma$ scenario over the small-$g_c$ scenario and that the parameter set that minimizes the cost function yields good agreement with the experimental structure factor and susceptibility, and qualitative agreement with the specific heat. The combination of Bayesian optimization and accurate low-energy solvers provides an effective approach for determining parameters of spin Hamiltonians. This methodology opens a systematic route to determining spin Hamiltonians in quantum magnets from experimental data.

item.title: [8] Dichotomous electronic system in a bilayer Ni1+ nickelate
item.description:
Last authors: K. -W. Lee, W. E. Pickett

Authors: Young-Joon Song, K. -W. Lee, W. E. Pickett

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Important electronic structure study of nickelates, relevant to correlated materials reader profile.

Tags: #nickelate #Fermisurface #electronic-structure

Abstract: "Infinite layer" nickelates ${\cal R}$NiO$_2$ (${\cal R}$=rare earth), having empty apical O sites, become superconducting upon hole doping, stimulating research into the related sequence Nd$_{n+1}$Ni$^{+p}_n$O$_{2n+2}$, formal charge state $p$=1+$\frac{1}{n}$, $n$=2,3,4,...., with the $n$=5 member being found to be superconducting. The two layer system La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_{7-\delta}$, with $\delta$=0,$\frac{1}{2}$,1 ($p$=2.5,2,1.5) approaches the peak in the nickelate superconducting dome but shows no superconductivity. Newly reported La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_5$F reaches the Ni$^{1+}$ goal while, as we show, introducing a partially occupied electron band $E^*$, based on an interstitial density that extends over the three open "apical" layers and leads to a single cylindrical electron Fermi surface giving self-doping. The commonly inert Ni $d_{xz},d_{yz}$ orbitals partner with interstitial $E^*$ to provide an incipient non-analytic Dirac point, with the critical point being reachable by pressure or further F insertion. The $E^*$ electron cylinder and the conventional Ni $dp\sigma$ hole carriers combine to provide a two-fluid dichotomy of hole and electron quasiparticles, affecting normal state properties that should verify the dichotomous aspect of transport.

item.title: [9] Magnetic Field Control of the N\'eel Vector and Magnon Visibility in Altermagnetic MnTe
item.description:
Last authors: Na Hyun Jo, Denis Karaiskaj

Authors: Tobias Weber, Niclas Heinsdorf, Shane Smolenski, et al.

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Direct experimental study (neutron scattering) of altermagnetism, very relevant to current interests.

Tags: #altermagnet #neutronscattering #magnon

Abstract: Altermagnetic order gives rise to momentum-dependent spin splitting of electronic and magnonic excitations even in the absence of a net magnetization. Here, we investigate the magnetic field dependence of the spin-wave spectrum of altermagnetic $\alpha$-MnTe using inelastic neutron scattering and linear spin-wave theory. An in-plane magnetic field continuously reorients the N\'eel vector by overcoming the weak crystalline anisotropy, while remaining small compared with the dominant exchange scale. We find that this reorientation leaves the magnon energies and line widths essentially unchanged, but strongly modifies the measured spectral intensity through the transverse-momentum projection. Our results demonstrate a clear separation between the soft orientational degree of freedom of the antiferromagnetic order and the robust exchange-dominated chiral magnon spectrum. This combination establishes $\alpha$-MnTe as a platform for reconfigurable magnon coupling, in which external fields tune how excitations interact with polarized probes without substantially altering their frequency or coherence.

item.title: [8] Extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity in the hole-doped Hubbard model
item.description:
Last authors: Si-Jing Du, Garnet Kin-Lic Chan

Authors: Ao Chen, Johnnie Gray, Si-Jing Du, Garnet Kin-Lic Chan

Score 8/10 C_MAYBE

Why: State-of-the-art computational study of stripe/superconductivity competition in cuprates.; tier capped to C: formal/generic theory watch

Tags: #cuprate #superconduct #Hubbard

Abstract: The two-dimensional Hubbard model was originally proposed as the minimal model of uniform $d$-wave superconductivity in the cuprate high-temperature superconductors, but recent calculations with relevant parameters in a realistic doping regime have often found other ground states. Further, uncertainty remains over such results due to the intrinsic bias of different computational methods. Here we address this uncertainty through state-of-the-art neural tensor network and neural backflow state simulations, enabled by large-scale GPU computation, that together reach an unprecedented variational accuracy on lattices with up to 1024 sites. At $1/8$ doping in the pure Hubbard model, as well as with next-nearest-neighbor hopping relevant to the hole-doped cuprates, we reveal a near degeneracy among a low-energy uniform $d$-wave state, superconducting stripes, and non-superconducting stripe states on the milli-$t$ energy scale. Our work rebalances the narrative that the Hubbard model supports a single dominant order in relevant parameter regimes towards a picture of extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity.
